findings.title: The scripts guide lists only three of twelve registered generated-surface families

evidence.note: Presents a list containing three generator families as the current checked-in generated surfaces.

evidence.measurement: 12 controls have a generatedSurface facet at the pin; only 3 of the 12 generator families appear in scripts/README.md, measured by selecting .controls[] entries with .generatedSurface.
evidence.note: Omissions include the concurrency graph, baseline-conflict recipes, lint coverage map, lint guidance, hook timeouts, config surfaces, skill artifacts, smoke subjects, and restricted-disable rules.
The authoritative loader normalizes every generatedSurface facet into the active registry.
All registered records feed generated-file freshness diagnostics.

findings.problem: A contributor following the scripts guide can infer that only three generator families require manifest-first maintenance and freshness checks. Nine active families are invisible, while a nongenerated demo is included in the same list.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat harness.controls.json and generated-surfaces.ts as authoritative. Generate a compact producer/output/refresh/check catalog, or label the current list as examples and link to a complete inventory.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-34 schedules other scripts/README layout corrections; it does not cover the nine omitted registered generator families.

findings.title: The drift:ai operator guide is an 890-line multi-audience README

evidence.note: Defines the external-repository quickstart.
Repeats the foreign-repository command, tools-checkout model, dependency installation, and canonical invocation.
Contains more than 300 lines of per-check implementation and calibration rationale.
Mixes prototype indexing, Musi-only integration, update instructions, known gaps, and archive status.

evidence.measurement: 890 lines, 7,176 words, 33 H2/H3 headings, and four separated external-invocation narratives at lines 18-72, 128-134, 235-300, and 628-685; measured from the pinned blob with wc, heading scans, and full reading.
evidence.note: One document serves portable onboarding, exhaustive reference, design rationale, Musi integration, and historical status.
Parity assertions pin README inventories and links against live registries.

findings.problem: An external operator must navigate an exhaustive maintainer reference whose supported invocation is restated four times. Registry changes, implementation rationale, Musi-only behavior, and archived status all churn one document and multiply its drift surfaces.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the live registries and parity assertions as authoritative. Keep a short README with one quickstart; move the portable contract, detailed check reference, Musi integration, and historical rationale into audience-specific documents.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-35 schedules an internal MODULE map; this finding separates public documentation audiences without restructuring the implementation forbidden by CQ25-146.

findings.title: The concurrency rulebook mislocates participant policy and misnames its ordering

evidence.note: Locates updateParticipant in routers/encounter.ts and describes character and participant lock families as code-point ordered.
Says PARTICIPANT_FIELD_KIND lives in routers/encounter.ts.
The router procedure is a one-line delegation to the encounter-combat service.
The service owns the exhaustive PARTICIPANT_FIELD_KIND map.
The service implements the request-facing updateParticipant writer.
The authoritative comparator explicitly implements UTF-16 code-unit order and distinguishes it from code-point order.

findings.problem: The central guide sends maintainers to a facade for the race-sensitive writer, names the wrong home for its fail-closed field map, and uses technically false terminology inside its lock-order argument.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat participant-action.ts and compareCodeUnits as authoritative. Point the writer and policy entries to the service and consistently describe the ordering as UTF-16 code-unit order, noting that current ASCII identifiers make the orders equivalent.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-21 schedules the same ordering terminology correction for the spell facade and MODULE; this finding adds the separate concurrency guide and its stale writer locations.

findings.title: Server contributor maps contradict or omit three important ownership boundaries

evidence.note: Categorically assigns business logic to services and says routers stay thin.
The more specific contract deliberately assigns per-entry validation and fail-fast error construction to the homebrew router.
The socket collaborator map omits persistence.
The room handler directly imports the singleton Prisma client alongside its injected PresenceService.

evidence.measurement: 46 non-test TypeScript files, 18 test files, 21 JSON assets, and no root MODULE.md or README at the pin; measured with git ls-tree.
evidence.note: The directory mixes runtime seeders, generated outputs, parsers, four generators, two backfills, and vendored data without a local orientation map.
The thirteen-step runtime seed order is encoded only as an imperative call list.

findings.problem: The server's local orientation system gives incompatible router-layering rules, hides a socket handler's persistence dependency, and provides no map for the large mixed-role seed subsystem. New contributors must reconstruct the actual boundaries from implementation imports and call order.
findings.proposedDirection: Split the repair by boundary: define the homebrew validation exception or move it consistently; document campaign-room membership reads; and add a seed map covering runtime order, generated ownership, generators, backfills, and existing operator guides.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-220 settles seed-pipeline implementation caveats; this finding preserves them and adds contributor orientation plus unrelated homebrew and socket documentation gaps.

findings.title: Shared local documentation carries stale test, consumer, and rules-provenance claims

evidence.note: Lists magic-item-inputs.ts among nine files without colocated tests.
The colocated test directly imports and substantively exercises magic-item-inputs.ts.
Names map-canvas-overlays.tsx as a direct consumer and omits map-canvas-store.ts.
The store directly imports TemplateShape from the shared area-template module.
The overlay imports the store-owned map tool and template mapping instead of the shared module.
Calls the CR-to-XP source 'SRD 5.1 / 2024 revision.'
The exhaustive independent oracle identifies SRD 5.2.1 as authoritative and checks every production table entry.

findings.problem: Three contributor-facing claims are contradicted by colocated tests, pinned imports, or an exhaustive rules oracle. The volatile hand-maintained inventories became stale after routine changes.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the colocated test, import graph, and SRD 5.2.1 oracle as authoritative. Correct the three claims and replace volatile exact inventories with checked or less brittle descriptions where practical.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed client cluster centralized the template-tool mapping; this finding identifies the remaining stale shared MODULE edge plus unrelated test and provenance drift.

findings.title: Client component MODULE documents misstate composition and feature ownership

evidence.note: Claims VttSurface composes the action bar and target-pick overlay.
VttSurface renders only its children and InVttDrawer.
The entire module document is a purpose sentence and three ownership bullets.

evidence.measurement: 14 tracked production TypeScript/TSX files totaling 1,888 lines at the pin, excluding tests, helpers, and MODULE.md; measured from the pinned git tree.
evidence.note: The stateful feature lacks data-flow, entry-point, state-ownership, test-seam, and gotcha guidance required by the module charter.
Advertises RollModeToggle as active UI and says combat owns log paging.

evidence.measurement: Zero production imports or references outside the defining file at the pin, measured with git grep excluding tests and MODULE.md.
evidence.note: The documented production consumer does not exist.
The panel receives a complete logs array and owns expansion state, not cursor or paging state.

findings.problem: Three high-change component maps are unreliable in different ways: one attributes composition to the wrong component, one is too thin to orient work, and one advertises production-dead UI plus nonexistent paging ownership.
findings.proposedDirection: Refresh each MODULE from the pinned composition and import graph. Preserve the existing VTT directory split, document the encounter data/mutation/state flow, and distinguish combat-log presentation from fetching and paging.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-190 cites the VTT MODULE wording while refusing a configurable shared shell; this finding corrects the wording without reopening that direction and adds separate encounter/combat documentation drift.

findings.title: Client hook and page entry-point maps omit major production surfaces

evidence.note: The External Entry Points section lists 18 names but omits active provider, invalidation, dashboard, and map-layer exports.

evidence.measurement: At least 8 production-consumed runtime exports are absent: AuthProvider, SocketProvider, useRealtimeInvalidationSubscription, useBackgroundImage, useCharacterActions, useMapLayerMutations, getLayerOfType, and SRD_LOOKUP_FALLBACK; measured by fixed-symbol git grep over non-test client production files.
evidence.note: The omissions span bootstrap, reconnect invalidation, dashboard actions, and map persistence.
The External Entry Points section names only two route-page exports and labels a private component external.

evidence.measurement: 13 non-test top-level *-page.tsx files export Page components; 11 of those route-facing exports are absent from MODULE.md, measured from the pinned tree and export declarations.
evidence.note: Most route pages cannot be discovered through the advertised entry-point index.
CampaignTabs is file-private despite being labeled an external entry point.

findings.problem: The only local maps for a 42-file hook tree and the route-page directory are partial without declaring an inclusion rule. They omit important architectural seams while presenting a private symbol as importable.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat production exports and imports as authoritative. Separate complete public/export inventories from internal landmarks and either generate them or document a stable inclusion rule.

findings.title: Client source comments preserve three superseded integration contracts

evidence.note: Says onFinalize receives a pre-mutation store snapshot although its signature accepts no argument.
The dispatcher invokes onFinalize with no snapshot.
Documents three filters as socket-hook surfaces and constructs them for every caller.

evidence.measurement: characterFilter, spellsFilter, and inventoryFilter each have zero non-test production reads outside their declarations and initializer, measured by fixed-symbol git grep over packages/client/src.
evidence.note: The socket-use explanation no longer matches the production reference graph.
The JSON assertion comment cites nonexistent packages/server/src/routes/uploads.ts.
The actual upload route declares the cited success response contract.

findings.problem: The comments describe a removed callback argument, an abandoned socket-filter design, and a nonexistent server file. Each obscures the current boundary precisely where the prose is intended to justify it.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the TypeScript signatures, production reference graph, and upload-routes.ts as authoritative. Correct the comments; route removal of the unused CharacterKeys members to the client implementation lane.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The finished client query-layer cluster did not remove the three now-unread socket-labeled CharacterKeys members; the canvas and upload comments are separate new paths.

findings.title: Root and devcontainer Compose bootstrap from ungoverned duplicate SQL

evidence.note: Root Compose mounts the root init-test-db.sql into PostgreSQL initialization.
Devcontainer Compose independently mounts its local copy at the same container path.
The root asset contains the same comments and two database-creation statements as the devcontainer copy, including a devcontainer-specific post-create reference.

evidence.measurement: The two 12-line SQL files are the same pinned Git blob, 083577183b7044314d060e11c051ca3c82954c0e; no non-agent-notes source references an equality or generation check.
evidence.note: Their equality is manual duplication rather than an enforced relationship.

findings.problem: Two independently mounted bootstrap assets can drift while both remain syntactically valid, producing different test-database availability between root Compose and the devcontainer. The root copy already carries prose specific to the other environment.
findings.proposedDirection: Choose one canonical SQL asset where portability permits, or generate/check both copies from one source so the standalone devcontainer remains reusable without creating an unguarded fork.

findings.title: Lint-ratchet newcomer docs omit a prerequisite and point to a deleted ruling

evidence.note: The Requirements section lists only Bun and a Git-tracked checkout.
The adoption recipe instructs each clone to run the merge-driver installer.
The installer invokes flock before writing Git configuration and attributes.
A live zone-policy comment cites a deleted leaf and describes moving the engine to tools/lint-ratchet as future work.
The live policy already covers tools/lint-ratchet/**/*.ts.
The retained index says the cited leaf was removed and records the landed zone-cap outcome.

findings.problem: An external adopter can satisfy every documented requirement yet fail during installation because flock is undeclared. Separately, maintainers reviewing the exceptional lint zone are sent to a deleted file and told an already-completed package move is pending.
findings.proposedDirection: Document flock with platform guidance and a preflight. Rewrite the lint-policy comment in present tense and link the retained landed record instead of the deleted leaf.
